hero.title: Decline of Buddhism and Jainism
hero.description: An analysis of the socio-religious and political transformation that led to the waning influence of heterodox sects in ancient India.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Critical phases marking the transition from heterodox dominance to the resurgence of Puranic Hinduism.

cards.details: Emergence of Buddhism and Jainism as a reaction against Vedic ritualism and the varna system.
Mauryan patronage (Ashoka) and trade route-based expansion (Kushan era).
Assimilation into Hinduism, loss of royal patronage, and destruction of institutions.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks to Remember
mnemonics.description: Use the mnemonic 'R.I.S.E.N' to remember the causes of decline.

items.title: R.I.S.E.N
items.decryption: R: Royal patronage shift; I: Internal schisms; S: Sanskrit vs Pali; E: External invasions (Hunas/Turks); N: Neo-Brahmanism (Puranic revival).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Buddhism did not disappear overnight due to external invasion alone; it was a long process of assimilation.
Avoid the misconception that Jainism declined solely due to lack of royal support; its strict asceticism limited mass conversion.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Drivers

  • Loss of Royal Patronage
  • Assimilation into Puranic Hinduism
  • Internal Institutional Decay

Key Factors

  • Language Shift (Pali/Prakrit to Sanskrit)
  • Monastic Corruption
  • Rise of Devotional Bhakti

Structural Analysis

  • Internal Weakness:
    • Loss of original focus (Monastic wealth accumulation).
    • Doctrinal divisions (Hinayana/Mahayana).
  • External Challenges:
    • Resurgence of Brahmanical traditions (Vedanta, Bhakti movement).
    • Institutional damage by invading forces (Hunas, Turks).
CauseImpact on BuddhismImpact on Jainism
LanguageShift to Sanskrit alienated massesRetained Prakrit but limited appeal
PatronageLost after Gupta/Post-Gupta eraMaintained through merchant guilds
